title: Arbitrator for dedicated-first routing with hosted spillover safeguards
creator: Lena Chen
description: Design and implement a routing arbitrator service that enforces 'dedicated-first' policies while applying host-side safeguards when spilling over to hosted. The arbitrator must evaluate region affinity, tier constraints, per-tenant reservations, and model-variant compatibility before releasing traffic to hosted. It should produce a small, explainable decision record for observability and replay. Work includes: policy spec, runtime enforcement hooks, telemetry events, fallback modelling for cheaper/quantized variants, integration tests and a canary rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Arbitrator evaluates requests against dedicated reservations and returns binding decision: {route: dedicated|hosted, variant: name, reason: string}
Hosted spillover occurs only when capacity, latency SLO and cost windows are satisfied per tenant policy
Fallback model variant selection enforces quality delta threshold and quantization whitelist
End-to-end tests simulating region outages, dedicated saturation and variant-degradation pass in CI
Decision logs are visible in Console trace pane and map to runbook playbooks

notes: Trade-offs: pushing more logic into arbitrator reduces per-node complexity but creates a single reasoning component; mitigations include horizontal sharding and read-only caches for the hot decision table.
We deliberately separate route decision (arbitrator) from enforcement (proxy layer) so we can run canary decisions without effecting production traffic during rollout.
Cost/latency trade: prefer dedicated with higher latency variance if it meets latency SLO for that tenant; prefer hosted when dedicated admission would push 99th percentile beyond threshold.

Runbook excerpt: when regional dedicated cluster enters 'degraded', arbitrator should demote dedicated affinity with exponential backoff and enable hosted-spillover only for tenants with allowed_spillover = true.
